def tree_of(path):
    return ast.parse(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read(), path)


def imports(path):
    out = []
    for n in ast.walk(tree_of(path)):
        if isinstance(n, ast.Import):
            out += [a.name for a in n.names]
        elif isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom):

def top(m):

def classes(path):

def functions(path):

## Function Command Line

main(argv=None, rpc=None, sleep=None) -> exit code. Global --db PATH (default ethsc.sqlite) before the subcommand. Without rpc, builds RpcClient(infura_url()), but only on the way into a subcommand that talks to the chain -- listen and backfill. Every other subcommand runs with INFURA_API_KEY unset and no .env in sight, and infura_url() is not called at all, so its RpcError never reaches the caller as a traceback. sleep=None means time.sleep, injected so listen can be stopped in a test. Entry point python -m ethsc: ethsc/__main__.py is a thin sys.exit(main()).

Behaviour: Output is plain text, one record per line, tab-separated, fully ordered; every float is printed "%.4f", exact inside. Records: "ALERT\t<address>\t<seed_address>\t<label>\t<score>" from backfill, listen, recheck and seed add; clusters top (K default 20): "<level>\t<key>\t<member count>"; cluster <addr>: "<level>\t<key>\t<members comma-joined>\t<flags>", 0 or 1 line, where <flags> is the risk flags of the queried address's code; similar: "<address>\t<score>\t<flags>"; risk: "<address>\t<flags>", one line per stored address whose code has at least one flag; seed list: "<address>\t<label>". A <flags> field is the set risk flags of that address's code as risk_flags gives them, the names that are True joined by "," in the fixed order selfdestruct then mutable_delegatecall, or "-" when neither is set (never an empty field); on cluster and similar it is always present, "-" included, so the record keeps a fixed column count. stdout holds only these records; stderr only one-line messages. Exit codes: 0 success; 1 RpcError out of follow_chain (stderr is str(err), no traceback); 2 usage error (argparse, a positional address not matching ^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$, seed add on an address without code) and main returns argparse's code instead of raising SystemExit; 3 when a budget or cap stop left work undone, and then one line goes to stderr: "stopped: <budget|cap>, spent <credits> credits, progress <block>", where <block> is "none" when no block has ever completed and <credits> is the ledger of the day the pass last charged (summary day), not of the day it started on. The ALERT lines of a block are written and flushed as that block ends, through the on_alerts sink of follow_chain, not gathered until the pass returns: under nohup an alert must reach the log before the next block is fetched, and it must survive a pass that never returns. The returned summary alerts are therefore not printed a second time. listen is a loop of follow_chain passes with sleep(interval) between them (interval default 12); a code 3 stop ends the loop. KeyboardInterrupt anywhere in listen or backfill is a clean stop -- exit 0, no traceback, progress of the last complete block kept, the unfinished block resumed on the next start -- and anywhere means the sleep, inside a pass (a transport call, a retry backoff), while the ALERT lines are being written, while the stop line is being written, and between a pass and the pause. recheck prints the alerts of recheck_watchlist(store, min_score=--min, 0.8 by default) over the whole database, one ALERT line each, in the order that function returns them, and exits 0 -- also with no seeds, no alerts or an empty database, where stdout stays empty. seed add, after a successful add_seed, prints the ALERT lines of recheck_watchlist(store, seed_addresses=[the new address]) at the fixed threshold 0.8: the copies of the new seed already in the database, which no listen or backfill will ever report again; its exit code stays 0, and a seed add that fails still exits 2 with an empty stdout.
